court: High Court of Judicature at Madras

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sathish Kumar, seeking restitution of conjugal rights

facts_of_case: The respondent filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, seeking restitution of conjugal rights after his wife left him. The trial court allowed the petition and the respondent appealed.

legal_principles.principle: Registration of Hindu marriages under Section 8 does not confer legitimacy to the marriage if there has been no marriage in accordance with Section 7.
legal_principles.held: The registration would not confer legitimacy to the marriage. There has to be a Hindu marriage in accordance with Section 7 of the Act.
cited_cases: Dolly Rani V. Manish Kumar Chanchal, (2024) 3 CTC 551

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu marriage must be solemnized in accordance with Section 7 of the Act for it to be considered a valid Hindu marriage.
legal_principles.held: There must be a 'Hindu marriage' in accordance with Section 7 of the Act, i.e., solemnization of such a marriage.
cited_cases: Dolly Rani V. Manish Kumar Chanchal, (2024) 3 CTC 551

outcome.final_order: The impugned order of the Court below was confirmed.

use_for_drafting: advising on restitution of conjugal rights
